dedupe_keys.name: global plastics ai policy tool machine learning projections of plastic flows waste fate and ghg under policy scenarios

description: This tool projects how much plastic the world will produce, use and throw away in future years, where that waste ends up, and how policies such as recycling targets or limits on mismanaged waste would change the result. The producers are A. Pottinger and Ciera Martinez of the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center for Data Science and Environment at the University of California, Berkeley, with Roland Geyer, Nivedita Biyani, Neil Nathan and Molly Morse of the University of California, Santa Barbara. It uses machine learning models trained on a snapshot of global plastics statistics to predict business-as-usual flows by region, sector and end-of-life fate, applies a policy engine with options such as minimum recycling rates, minimum recycled content, a cap on mismanaged waste and investment in recycling or incineration, and calculates greenhouse gas emissions by polymer, with Monte Carlo runs for uncertainty. Coverage is global, broken into regions. The archive holds outputs, documentation for the model and each policy, the data and training pipeline, emission code and the interactive tool, and is available as a free download from Zenodo under the BSD 3-Clause licence, with the tool online. Caveats: projections rest on historical statistics and chosen model structures, and regional detail is coarse. Simulation uses: estimating future plastic waste loads on collection, sorting and disposal systems under policy options. Related records: ODYM (model-odym) builds material flow models, and the Europe polymer flows (data-europe-polymer-dynamic-probabilistic-mfa) give European detail.
inputs: Snapshot of upstream plastics production, trade, consumption and waste data as a SQLite database
Policy settings such as minimum recycling (collection) rate, minimum recycled content, maximum mismanaged rate, recycling and incineration investment
